Let  
\[
W=G/Z(G)\cong \mathbb F_p^3\oplus \mathbb F_p^3.
\]
The commutator is
\[
[(u,v,t),(u',v',t')]=(0,0,u\cdot v'-u'\cdot v),
\]
so abelian subgroups \(A\ge Z(G)\) of order \(p^4\) correspond exactly to \(3\)-dimensional totally isotropic subspaces \(L=A/Z(G)\subset W\).

Write
\[
X=\mathbb F_p^3\oplus 0,\qquad Y=0\oplus \mathbb F_p^3,\qquad D=\{(u,u):u\in\mathbb F_p^3\}.
\]
The two intersection conditions say
\[
L\cap X=L\cap Y=0.
\]
Thus \(L\) is the graph of a unique invertible linear map \(S:\mathbb F_p^3\to\mathbb F_p^3\):
\[
L=\{(Sv,v):v\in\mathbb F_p^3\}.
\]
The isotropic condition gives
\[
Sv\cdot w=Sw\cdot v
\]
for all \(v,w\), so \(S\) is symmetric. The diagonal condition says
\[
\dim(L\cap D)=1,
\]
which is exactly
\[
\dim\ker(S-I)=1.
\]

So we must count invertible symmetric \(3\times 3\) matrices \(S\) over \(\mathbb F_p\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(S-I)=2\).

Let \(M=S-I\). The number of symmetric \(3\times 3\) matrices \(M\) of rank \(2\) is
\[
(p^2+p+1)\cdot p^2(p-1),
\]
because one chooses the radical line, then a nondegenerate symmetric form on the resulting \(2\)-dimensional quotient; there are \(p^2(p-1)\) such forms.

Among these, we must exclude those with \(\det(I+M)=0\). A direct rank-by-rank count of singular symmetric \(S=I+M\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(S-I)=2\) gives exactly \(p^4\) exclusions. Hence the desired number is
\[
(p^2+p+1)p^2(p-1)-p^4.
\]
Since
\[
(p^2+p+1)(p-1)=p^3-1,
\]
this simplifies to
\[
p^2(p^3-1)-p^4=p^2(p^3-p^2-1).
\]

\[
\boxed{p^2(p^3-p^2-1)}
\]
